newsitem.title: UK: Coffee growers to maintain grip on exports.
newsitem.headline: Coffee growers to maintain grip on exports.

text.p: The world's major coffee growers decided on Saturday to maintain a tight grip on exports to prevent an oversupply.

The 14-member Association of Coffee Producing Countries, meeting in London, made no policy changes and said it would limit coffee exports for the year to June 1997 to the 53.5 million 60-kg bags agreed on in May.
Exports for the year ended last June were 44 million bags, slightly below the 45.8 million bag limit it set in the first year of the new programme, the ACPC said.
"There was a shortfall of 2.19 percent of the target and this is seen as positive by the member countries," ACPC president Rubens Antonio Barbosa of Brazil told reporters.
ACPC officials said no new initiatives were in the pipeline.
"The idea is just to continue with the second export programme...there are no new proposals," ACPC secretary-general Robeiro Oliviera Silva, also of Brazil, said.
But Oliviera said he did not discount the possibility of revising supply controls if prices continue to tumble.
Coffee prices are hovering at $1,500 a tonne, down from nearly $2,000 in May. They peaked at $4,000 in 1994, when frosts and drought hit Brazil, the world's top grower.
Delegates also criticised the European Union over a proposal to classify coffee according to the country where it is processed.
The EU, which grows no coffee of its own, is considering the suggestion that if coffee is processed beyond a certain degree in an EU country it should be labelled as originating there.
ACPC delegates said the proposal could undermine "the very fabric of the coffee culture".
"We are very concerned about the proposed changes. We maintain that the origin of coffee is where it is produced," one producer delegate said.
